newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise gently, peso bonds ahead.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise gently, peso bonds ahead.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Friday with peso denominated paper leading the way.
The market treaded water for much of the session but managed to put in gentle gains in the afternoon as the still mainly positive sentiment of late held sway, traders said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.08 to 120.78, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 gained 1/4 to 85.
The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 rose 35 centavos to 93.
Trade remained thin, said market players.
In spite of the overwhelming feeling of confidence in the market, its gains were slight this week. The "Pre 2" stood at 120.35 a week ago while the "Pro 1" was at 93, unchanged from five days ago.
The chief trader at an Argentine bank said "I don't see explosive gains, but I am long on the market."

"What is missing for real market gains are foreign flows," said an analyst at an Argentine bank, echoing comments by traders in recent sessions. Still, the continued low participation of investors meant the market had one of its lowest volatility levels in a long time this week, added the analyst.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.0 percent from 6.15 percent.
